mappings.note: What the child sees - a stated detail. LO-197; rejected LO-198, which is for responses needing inference.

Alliteration: find the matching consonant pairs in two stanzas, then invent four sets. Cited at competency level because the 16-outcome Class 6 frame has no poetic-device outcome - C-ENG1.1 is the competency that owns poems and their sound. Rejected its LO-194 ('Recite and share poems... tongue twisters') because nothing is recited, and LO-203, which is about meaning rather than sound.
What the kites 'symbolize' is never stated; a figurative reading, so LO-198 over LO-197.
What the child does not wish to be is stated in the poem. LO-197 detail retrieval.

Asks how the opening two lines describe the kites - locating what the text says, LO-197. NB the supplied key is generic ('often describes the kites with vivid imagery') and does not quote the lines; a weak answer key rather than a wrong one.
The wish to be small and light is stated. LO-197.
Requires scanning the poem to find which motion verb is ABSENT - locating details, LO-197. Rejected LO-203: the pupil is not glossing the words, only checking which appear.
The speaker's excitement about flying is stated. LO-197 detail retrieval.
What the child will do on the kite is stated (listen to the song). LO-197.
Asks what 'paper wings' refers to - working out a metaphor's referent from its context, LO-203. Rejected LO-197, which would cover only the literal kite.

Applies the themes to modern life, well past the poem; LO-198 with LO-206.
